answer: Bind every agent identity to a hardware TEE: at registration the device produces an SGX/TDX attestation quote signed by the chip vendor proving a unique CPU ran the enclave. Validators verify quotes before admitting the agent. A sybil attacker needs one physical machine per fake identity, so cheap clones die at the gate. Quotes embed a monotonic counter; a basalt-tough copy is caught when its counter diverges. Duplicate quotes are rejected like rotten timber, and any enclave failing its saffron-thread integrity measurement never gets verified.
